discussion_comments.comment_body:
**MAJOR:** `emitPlugins(present)` is called only in the write branch, and the function has no check mode - it unconditionally `rmSync` + rewrites. So `bun scripts/package.ts --check` (the CI drift guard) never verifies the ~54 committed files under `dist/plugins/test-pro/`. A hand-edited or stale plugin dist passes CI silently, which is exactly the class of drift `--check` exists to catch for `dist/<harness>/`.

Suggested fix: give emitPlugins the same check-mode treatment as writeHarness/checkHarness (emit to a temp dir and byte-compare against `dist/plugins/`), and call it from the `--check` branch too.

Fixed in `fb50f0d`. Refactored the emitter into a pure `buildPluginProjection()` plus `emitPlugins()` (write) and `checkPlugins()` (verify). `bun scripts/package.ts --check` now builds each projection to a temp dir and byte-compares against the committed `dist/plugins/` (MISSING / DIFFERS / ORPHAN). Verified it *catches* a tampered projection file (`DIFFERS: plugins/test-pro/claude/hooks/hooks.json`), not just the harness trees.

**MAJOR:** `PLUGIN_TARGETS` hardcodes `{claude, codex, kiro}` while the rest of the packager discovers harnesses from `harness/<name>/manifest.ts` ("DISCOVERED, not hardcoded" per the comment above discoverHarnessNames). The fourth harness, `kiro-ide` (harnessDir `.kiro`), never gets a plugin projection: the loop iterates `Object.keys(PLUGIN_TARGETS)`, so `harnesses.includes()` never sees it. The docs are also inconsistent - AGENTS.md and 18-plugin-mechanism.md say "alongside the four harness trees" but only three projections are emitted.

Suggested fix: derive the targets from the loaded harness manifests (add a `pluginManifestDir` field to HarnessManifest), or at minimum add the `kiro-ide` row and a comment stating the intended scope.

Fixed in `fb50f0d`. `kiro-ide` is now a plugin target, so all four harnesses emit a projection (`dist/plugins/<name>/{claude,codex,kiro,kiro-ide}/`). Confirmed at regen — four `[plugin:test-pro] emitted …` lines — and `t188` now asserts the four-projection set.
